title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## MuTRAP & PROTEA Security Demo

### The Breakthrough
Researchers introduced MuTRAP, a multi‑trigger Trojan that inserts secret keywords (e.g., "CF") into an LLM planner, causing a Segway‑based robot to switch from cutting an apple to cutting a model hand on demand. They also built PROTEA, an LLM‑based monitor that evaluates each planned step against the evolving environment and flags unsafe actions, achieving reasonable detection accuracy on the physical demo.

### The Caveats
The work provides no comparison to existing security baselines, leaving it unclear whether PROTEA truly outperforms prior defenses.

## AdaDex Dexterous Mimicking

### The Breakthrough
AdaDex combines dense motion‑tracking objectives with sparse object‑success rewards in parallel environments, turning a few seconds of human hand‑object motion into a single policy that can imitate and generalize. The hybrid training yields adaptable dexterous skills such as finger gaiting, in‑hand reorientation, and dynamic throw‑and‑catch, and transfers from simulation to a real robot hand.

### The Caveats
The paper fails to name baseline methods for comparison, so the reported improvement cannot be independently verified.

## Digit 5 Warehouse Humanoid

### The Breakthrough
Agility Robotics unveiled Digit 5, a bipedal robot with two arms optimized for lifting 23 kg bins onto high shelves, running for 90 minutes after a 9‑minute rapid charge. The system reuses reinforcement‑learning‑derived controllers from Cassie to achieve high‑throughput warehouse shifts.

### The Caveats
The claim of commercial‑grade warehouse performance is unsupported because no quantitative success‑rate, cycle‑time, safety, or long‑term reliability metrics are provided.

## Bolt Lucid Robotaxi with Nvidia Alpamayo

### The Breakthrough
Bolt announced that its future fleet of at least 25,000 Lucid robotaxis will run Nvidia's Alpamayo self‑driving stack, which blends "reasoning AI" with classic perception and planning on the Hyperion compute platform, and will be tuned on a Madrid data‑collection program starting in 2027.

### The Caveats
The promised fleet is based solely on an unverified company announcement, with no real‑world performance data or hardware‑in‑the‑loop validation.

## AgenticRoboRL Planner Boost

### The Breakthrough
AgenticRoboRL adds harness‑specific adapters and a training pipeline that mixes supervised fine‑tuning with multi‑turn reinforcement learning, raising LIBERO‑PRO success from 18.1% to 71.0% for a 9B‑parameter planner—close to the 72.1% of a much larger Codex model.

### The Caveats
The 71% success rate is demonstrated only in simulation on LIBERO‑PRO, with no hardware experiments to confirm real‑world transfer.

## UniWALM Unified Control Model

### The Breakthrough
UniWALM uses a single transformer with diffusion heads that jointly denoise video, action, and language streams, feeding generated language back as memory to handle compositional, memory‑heavy manipulation; it shows large gains on simulated pick‑and‑place benchmarks and a real‑world Find‑the‑Item task.

### The Caveats
The reported real‑world gains rely on a single Find‑the‑Item task, so it is unclear whether UniWALM’s advantages extend to other embodied robot tasks.

## Physical Canvas Vision‑Tactile Model

### The Breakthrough
PhysCanvas encodes RGB, tactile, marker displacement, and robot state into a shared video VAE, enabling optical‑touch simulation that lifts Pearson correlation between simulated and real success from 0.602 to 0.885 and improves post‑trained policy success from 59.1% to 70.8% on four real tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper never isolates the contribution of each modality nor compares against existing multimodal world‑model baselines, leaving the claimed advantage unverified.

## inspect‑robots Evaluation Framework

### The Breakthrough
inspect‑robots is a Python library offering a unified API for defining robotics benchmarks and running any policy (LLM agent, vision‑language‑action model, or scripted controller) on compatible robots or simulators, automatically logging sensor data and generating live visualizations via Rerun.

### The Caveats
The repository provides only a framework description with no empirical or hardware tests, so its claimed ability to evaluate arbitrary policies on real robots remains unverified.

### Priority
MuTRAP & PROTEA expose a concrete, hardware‑validated security flaw in LLM‑driven planners, making it the most urgent story for anyone deploying embodied AI today.

### One action
Audit your robot’s LLM planning pipeline for hidden trigger words or integrate a monitoring layer similar to PROTEA.

### What to watch
Several papers (AdaDex, AgenticRoboRL, UniWALM, Physical Canvas) push simulation‑to‑real transfer by coupling large‑scale learning with multimodal or language‑based representations. Watch how they evolve from pure simulation gains (AgenticRoboRL) toward real‑hand demonstrations (AdaDex) and integrated perception‑action‑language loops (UniWALM, PhysCanvas), which could reshape future embodied‑AI training pipelines.
